summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing process, reference architecture for a joint solution, metering & billing integration, and next steps to onboard Redwood as a SkyBridge marketplace offering.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-06-04 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marta Li (SkyBridge Partnerships), Jordan Reyes (SkyBridge DevRel), Samir Patel (SkyBridge Marketplace PM)

Auto-summary: quick tech sync to cover listing requirements, reference arch, SSO/KMS concerns, and sandbox testing plan.

00:00 Alex Romero: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we wanted to make sure we align on the end-to-end for getting Redwood onto SkyBridge marketplace, so a bit of agenda \u001F reference arch, metering & billing integration, SSO/entitlements, and test plan, sound good?
00:18 Marta Li: yeah sounds great, thanks Alex, quick note I'm on partnerships so I'll own go-to-market pieces but Samir and Jordan will handle the listing and technical bits.
00:30 Jordan Reyes: yep, and we want to make the listing as plug-and-play as possible for customers, minimize manual steps.
00:39 Priya Shah: cool, from Redwood SE side I'll walk through the recommended deployment patterns; we have two primary flows \u001F hosted API listing (Redwood hosted offering) and packaged private deployment (customer-managed via skybridge marketplace private offer).
00:55 Samir Patel: can you clarify what you mean by packaged private deployment? are we talking AMI/container marketplace images?
01:04 Priya Shah: yeah so for private we typically provide a terraform module and an optional container image plus Helm charts; customers can deploy in their VPC but we support a private listing that includes automated installers and a reference architecture doc. sometimes it's misunderstood as a full managed service, but it's really an on-prem/VPC package they run.
01:30 Jordan Reyes: got it, that maps to what we call \"bring-your-own-infra\" offers. For the listing we need artifact locations, deployment instructions, and a way to validate the install in CI. what's the minimal deliverable?
01:44 Priya Shah: minimal is: 1) reference architecture PDF, 2) terraform/helm repo link, 3) docker image or image manifest, 4) test harness that can run smoke checks against an endpoint, and 5) metadata for the marketplace (pricing skus, entitlement flags). We can provide example smoke tests.
02:05 Alex Romero: on pricing skus, Redwood will offer hosted per-token pricing and a private license SKU for reserved capacity \u001F we need your SKU templates so we can map our units to your metering.
02:18 Samir Patel: yep, SkyBridge uses metering hooks \u001F we can accept custom usage payloads or use marketplace metering. Do you have server-side metering events we can consume?
02:29 Priya Shah: yes, for hosted we already emit per-request metering via a webhook and we can push aggregated usage per account. For private/offline installs we typically integrate with a reporting agent that reports usage back to a collector \u001F there is a sliding window and signed payloads; we can share the spec.
02:45 Marta Li: good \u001F security is a big ask too. we require SOC2 or equivalent, plus documents for SSO/SAML, RBAC integration, and KMS notes. what do you have today?
02:57 Priya Shah: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, we have an audit pack (we'll attach), SAML SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments as well as our managed KMS for hosted. sometimes the acronyms get mixed \u001F we support HSM integrations via standard APIs.
03:18 Jordan Reyes: will that be enough for our marketplace security checklist?
03:22 Priya Shah: should be; we'll share a redwood-sec.zip with the SOC2, pen test summary, and a short KMS integration guide.
03:31 Samir Patel: perfect. Next, can we talk network topology for private installs \u001F e.g., does Redwood expect specific ports, NAT, or peering?
03:40 Priya Shah: minimal network: egress to pull images and allow telemetry to the collector (optional), inbound for the API if customers want direct access; for private we recommend internal load balancer + internal KV cache pinned to GPU nodes. If there's a strict air-gap we also provide an offline bundle but that's a separate program.
04:01 Jordan Reyes: ok, for our listing flow we need a diagram and a list of endpoints/ports \u001F can you include that in the reference arch?
04:07 Priya Shah: yes. we'll include port lists, recommended subnets, and a sample security group/NSG config.
04:14 Alex Romero: something else that comes up is model governance \u001F customers ask which models are available and whether they change over time; for marketplace we'll need a model catalog manifest that lists model variants, quantization levels, and SMB notes.
04:31 Priya Shah: we can produce a manifest.json that lists models, sizes, recommended seq lengths, and compatibility notes. small note \u001F transcriber sometimes converts KV cache to K-V cash but you'll see that in doc names, ha.
04:46 Jordan Reyes: laughter, noted.
04:51 Samir Patel: on the billing side, do you need us to call your metering endpoints in real time, or will batched reports suffice?
04:59 Priya Shah: batched daily reports with signed payloads work fine \u001F the hosted flow is near real time but for marketplace we'll accept daily aggregates. We do want alignment on ids \u001F account id mapping between SkyBridge and Redwood; Alex will coordinate mapping rules.
05:17 Alex Romero: yes I'll follow up with mapping schema.
05:21 Marta Li: another question \u001F product images and marketing \u001F do you want to co-brand or do you prefer neutral?
05:28 Alex Romero: co-brand is fine but we prefer Redwood-first with a SkyBridge badge; we'll share logos and short description copy.
05:36 Jordan Reyes: technical Q \u001F how do you handle upgrades and rollbacks for private installs that come from our marketplace images? customers expect a one-click upgrade flow on our console.
05:47 Priya Shah: we support canary rollouts via our helm charts and can provide a control-plane agent that the customer's infra can call; for marketplace one-click flows we can pull the new image and trigger helm upgrade \u001F we'll provide the necessary webhook hooks to surface progress back to your console. there are some caveats with long-lived KV caches when stateful model shards are in play.
06:12 Samir Patel: okay stateful shards \u001F anything we need to call out in the listing docs?
06:18 Priya Shah: call out model version pinning and note that warm-up may be required; also note recommended cache eviction policies. we'll include migration steps in the ref arch.
06:28 Jordan Reyes: perfect. next item \u001F sandbox testing. we need a plan for you to run smoke tests in our marketplace sandbox so we can approve the listing.
06:37 Priya Shah: proposed plan: Redwood provides a CI job (github action) that runs against your sandbox with test credentials; we run smoke tests (generation, embeddings, authorization checks) and produce a report. we will also provide a small sample dataset to validate latencies.
06:53 Jordan Reyes: that aligns with our QA. We'll need a list of endpoints and test credentials; Samir can provision.
06:58 Samir Patel: yes I'll provision sandbox accounts. expect to see emails from redwood-infra@redwood.ai.
07:05 Marta Li: on timelines, what's realistic to get a basic listing up?
07:10 Alex Romero: if we get the listing requirements doc today and sandbox access within a week, we can probably produce the ref arch and test harness in 7\u201310 days; listing approval may take another week. so roughly 3 weeks end-to-end for a basic hosted listing.
07:27 Jordan Reyes: fine. anything blocking from our side?
07:30 Marta Li: legal has a standard addendum for marketplace revenue share \u001F I'll loop legal in after this call.
07:37 Alex Romero: noted \u001F I'll send our standard marketplace contract template to speed things up.
07:43 Priya Shah: small technical nit \u001F for telemetry we can support both metric push and pull; which does SkyBridge prefer?
07:50 Samir Patel: we prefer push to our collector with signed JSON payloads.
07:54 Priya Shah: okay will align to that.
07:58 Jordan Reyes: competitors question \u001F we've had listings from CloudMart that use a similar pattern; anything you learned from those?
08:05 Alex Romero: yes, we learned to include explicit automated smoke checks and to include a customer-facing status page for upgrades; that reduces rejection loops.
08:16 Marta Li: good to know.
08:20 Jordan Reyes: any security red flags we should expect?
08:23 Priya Shah: only typical ones \u001F ensure KMS keys and service principals are documented, ensure RBAC mappings are clear. we'll provide a short runbook for incident response in the ref arch package.
08:36 Samir Patel: any monitoring hooks we should expose for your hosted offering?
08:41 Priya Shah: for hosted we do not expose internals, but we do provide observability endpoints for per-route latencies and per-token cost estimates via our API; for private we can ship metrics endpoints (Prometheus) that you can scrape.
08:58 Alex Romero: ok, let's do a short walkthrough of the reference arch slide then Priya can call out what she'll include.
09:05 Priya Shah: (screen share note) slide 1 \u001F high level: 3 blocks: Redwood control plane (for hosted) / customer infra (private) / SkyBridge marketplace meta. slide 2 \u001F network and KMS, slide 3 \u001F upgrade and metering flow, slide 4 \u001F CI smoke tests and acceptance criteria.
09:31 Priya Shah: details I'll include: port lists, helm values example, terraform snippet, model manifest example, metering payload spec (signed daily aggregate), security pack links, sample smoke test results, and a checklist for one-click upgrade integration.
09:50 Jordan Reyes: can you include sample logs we expect to see so our QA can validate?
09:55 Priya Shah: yes, sample logs and a sample smoke test report.
10:00 Marta Li: ok that should cover it. quick note on marketing copy \u001F we'll need 2\u20133 short blurbs. Alex will take that on?
10:08 Alex Romero: yes I'll draft 3 blurbs and send them to Marta by EOD Friday (2026-06-07).
10:15 Jordan Reyes: circling back to metering: are there any pii concerns with the usage payload?
10:20 Priya Shah: no PII in usage payloads \u001F just account id, timestamp, usage tokens, and hashes. we'll send the payload spec.
10:29 Samir Patel: good.
10:32 Marta Li: ok last thing \u001F acceptance for the marketplace listing requires documented rollback procedures and an SLA for the hosted offering. do you have SLA tiers?
10:42 Alex Romero: yes for hosted we have standard and enterprise tiers \u001F we'll share the SLA doc. private deployments get an enterprise support add-on.
10:51 Marta Li: great.
10:54 Alex Romero: okay quick recap of next steps: Priya will share ref arch draft by 6/11, Alex will send onboarding checklist and pricing SKU template by 6/7, Jordan will send listing schema by 6/9, Samir will provision sandbox by 6/10, Marta will loop legal on revenue share. anything else?
11:16 Jordan Reyes: that's it from me.
11:18 Priya Shah: one more thing \u001F we have an internal test harness that can run on your sandbox if you give us a service account; that will speed verification.
11:26 Samir Patel: will do.
11:29 Alex Romero: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the next workshop if needed.
11:35 Marta Li: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: minor transcription artifacts (e.g., \"KV cash\" instead of \"KV cache\"), some speaker labels abbreviated. Action items recorded above match the call recap.
